clue.text: Fair idea, say, settled heretical one

parts.note: say, for example, abbreviated eg
a bird that settled alit
Arianism was the early Christian heresy denying Christ's full divinity; the 'one' is another idea

explanation.surface: A theologian dismisses a supposedly fair notion as a settled heresy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'idea': a heretical idea, the doctrine of Arius.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief in equal rights and status for all people is a political principle of fairness.

clue.text: Sign union's promised to hire staff somewhere in Herts

parts.note: to engage workers is to hire them
staff, the workforce, are men
Tring is a small town in Hertfordshire, an English county north of London

explanation.surface: A trade union announces it has promised to take on workers at a site in Hertfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks industrial, beside 'hire staff', but it is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring given at a betrothal signals that a marriage has been pledged.

clue.text: Rising star drinking mixed gin in European city

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nova is a star that flares up

indicators.note: mixed means these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rising celebrity downs a gin cocktail in a continental city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns NOVA into AVON, which takes in IGN, the anagram of GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Avignon is a city in Provence, southern France, once home to the popes.

clue.text: Keen on catching Mahler's last prelude

indicators.note: catching means holding something within, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

indicators.note: the composer's last means only the final letter of his name is taken

explanation.surface: A music fan is keen on the opening of Mahler's final symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: A short introductory passage of music is informally called an intro, much like an overture.

clue.text: Short notice to include game

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an advertisement or notice is an ad
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A brief announcement adds a game to the programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortened text, cut down from the full version, is an abridged one.

clue.text: Like ring topped with cool colour

indicators.note: in a down clue, topped with means the next piece sits above the rest

parts.note: something cool or fashionable is in
to like something is to dig it, in slang
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A ring with a cool-coloured stone on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet shade of the rainbow.

clue.text: Drugs business jerks earlier sped up

indicators.note: earlier means this piece comes before the others
in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: sped means ran
CO is short for company, a business
tics are involuntary jerks

explanation.surface: A drug-dealing operation's thugs moved fast to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sped up' says RAN reads upwards, giving NAR, and 'earlier' places it first.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics are opiates and other illegal substances, the stock of a dealer.

clue.text: Replacement programme drops current story

parts.note: a sub is a substitute or replacement

indicators.note: drops means a letter is let fall out of the word

parts.note: a pilot is a trial programme for a TV series
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A replacement TV show abandons its contemporary storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'up to date' but is the physics symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary thread of narrative running alongside the main one is a kind of story.

clue.text: Cook comes with crisp or golden chip

indicators.note: to cook the books is to rearrange them, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A chef arrives with a crisp or a golden chip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chip' looks like a potato snack beside 'Cook' and 'crisp', but it is a silicon chip.
explanation.definitionFit: The central processing unit of a computer on a single silicon wafer is commonly called a chip.

clue.text: Was brilliant in golf, then made a mess

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to have littered is to have made a mess with rubbish

explanation.surface: A golfer played superbly, then fell apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sparkled or shone dazzlingly was brilliant in the literal sense.

clue.text: Community leader to go on endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to rabbit on is British slang for talking at length

explanation.surface: A local figurehead who never stops talking.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit is British slang for chattering on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish congregation is led by its religious teacher and minister.

clue.text: Almost left magical place, back in wild

indicators.note: almost means the word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: having left is to be gone

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: Oz is the magical land of The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: Someone nearly escaped from a fairy-tale land and returned to the wilderness.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour or journalism in this style is outlandish, bizarre and unrestrained.

clue.text: Fancy coral and gold adornment for the cloth

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An ornate coral-and-gold decoration for a fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' looks like fabric but is the clergy, whose white neckband this is.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth is an idiom for the clergy, and their stiff white collar marks their office.

clue.text: Handle British money on tick

indicators.note: on means this piece is placed after the next one

parts.note: a tick, a moment, is a mo
a nicker is British slang for a pound

explanation.surface: Buying with British cash on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tick' reads as British slang for credit, but tick is a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a person's name or nickname, as is this word.

clue.text: Copper on drug affair turned up dead ends

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
LSD is the hallucinogenic drug

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: a case is an affair or matter

explanation.surface: A police officer working a drugs case finds it leads nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Streets closed at one end are dead ends, literally the bottoms of bags in French.

clue.text: Quality of vessel with stone from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, from the east means read from right to left

parts.note: a pot is a vessel
a pit is the stone of a fruit

explanation.surface: A characteristic of a pot holding an Oriental stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Quality used as an adjective, as in quality goods, means excellent or first-rate.

clue.text: Saturated fat

definitions.meaning: soaked through, wet enough to drip
the fat that runs from roasting meat, used for cooking

explanation.surface: A dietary label for saturated fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaking wet means saturated, and the melted meat fat kept from a roast is the second sense.

clue.text: Extra swell? Quite!

parts.note: a swell, a toff, is a nob
quite as in completely, like 'all alone'

explanation.surface: Someone agrees heartily that something is an extra-fine thing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an illegal delivery gives the batting side an extra run, which cricket calls an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat, and an illegal delivery is one.

clue.text: Fit to include half of rulers' praise

indicators.note: to include means to take in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a fit, as of coughing, is a bout

indicators.note: half of means only the first half of the word is used

parts.note: queens are rulers

explanation.surface: Royal praise fit to include.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouquet is a compliment or tribute, figuratively an offering of flowers.

clue.text: True love overwhelms singular stage hero

indicators.note: overwhelms means engulfs, so a piece is swallowed inside

parts.note: proper means true or genuine
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A real romance overpowers a remarkable lead actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The magician-duke at the centre of Shakespeare's The Tempest is a leading character in a play.

clue.text: For one leader of gang, place for punishment that could become life?

parts.note: for one means for example, eg

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a prison cell is a place for punishment

explanation.surface: A gang boss in a prison cell might get a life sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'life' looks like a life sentence, but this is biological life.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertilised ovum develops into a new organism, so it could grow into a living being.

clue.text: State of book, one containing old letter

indicators.note: containing means holding inside

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
a rune is a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet

explanation.surface: A book that holds an ancient letter of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small sultanate on Borneo, a sovereign country.

clue.text: Drinks and drugs experience going both ways

parts.note: a round is drinks bought for a group
a trip is a hallucinogenic drug experience

explanation.surface: A night of drinking and drug-taking that runs in two directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A return journey, out and back, travels in both directions.

clue.text: Listen to the French horn

parts.note: to bug a phone is to listen in to it
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An instruction to hear the French horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French horn' reads as one instrument; the horn is separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle is a simple brass instrument like a valveless horn.

clue.text: Coming round, I love British or Russian food

indicators.note: coming round means turning round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: love is nothing in tennis, nil

explanation.surface: Recovering consciousness, someone declares a love of British or Russian dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Small buckwheat pancakes, served with caviar or sour cream, are a Russian dish.

clue.text: Mind introducing new terms

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: nous is mind or intellect

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out when bringing in new conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Words naming things are terms in grammar's naming sense.

clue.text: Prying about the setter's conspicuous quality

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: nosiness is prying
the setter refers to themselves as I; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: The crossword setter's notable trait is being nosy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being loud and clamorous is a characteristic that draws attention.

clue.text: Supply moving elfin girl is present

parts.note: a supply is stock

indicators.note: moving means the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: An elf girl carrying supplies is a Christmas present.
explanation.definitionFit: A small gift put in a Christmas stocking is a present.
